title: RWB-S6-E6005: the award step carries an empty C row although it consumes rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-access and rwb-source-data, and three consumed operations have no published name
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.3 and R9; WP B2-S6-008 story lines RWB-S6-E6005-APP and RWB-S6-E6005-CON (H, C, I, X); context pack S6 rwb-debtsale (ownership rows, slide 13); TSD S6 Debt sale v2 T5.2, T6.1 and T-A; FSD S6 Debt sale v3 A2.9; legacy RWB-E6-005
section: Metadata (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies); Sections 3, 4, 12.2, 12.8 and 13
description: (1) The plan gives H = RWB-S6-E6005-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON and C, I and X = None, while the step reads the P3 case state and answers the P3 case move, reads the P7 DS package and, above the DoA limit, starts the P7 approval chain, reads the P4 delegation_limit row and reads the P1 model score. (2) No source publishes an operation name for the package read, the score read or the case-move answer, so all three carry the placeholder. (3) The legacy Data table lists recovery_case, decision_log_entry, v_ace_score and rule_row as if they were the step's own data, and all four belong to P3, P7, P1 and P7 in the target.
evidence: WP B2-S6-008 story lines with H of three CON stories and empty C, I and X; Template and Rules v1 R5.4 class C (build against the published contract and its fake); context pack S6 ownership rows (5 REST operations, 1 event, DebtSaleWorkflow) and slide 13 matrix row S6 Debt sale (P7 T, P5 T, P8 E, P2 T); TSD S6 T5.2 and T6.1; FSD S6 A2.9.2 integration points (Workbench, Partner portal)
proposed: Declare the six consumed rows in 12.2 with their owners, their budget and the placeholder, fake them for the build, and keep the metadata C row as the plan states it

title: RWB-S6-E6005: the step publishes LotAwarded (EV-23) while DP-09 and its outbox library are absent from the plan's pattern set and H row
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.3 and R9; WP B2-S6-008 story lines RWB-S6-E6005-APP and -CON (patterns, H); context pack S6 rwb-debtsale (event row EV-23, slide 13 matrix); TSD S6 Debt sale v2 T5.3 and T-A; Architecture v5 slide 43; legacy RWB-E6-005
section: Metadata (Patterns applied, Depends on (build)); Sections 4, 8, 12.3, 12.7, 13 and 17
description: TSD S6 T5.3 publishes LotAwarded, the context pack carries one event for the service (EV-23), and the slide 13 matrix shows rwb-payment and rwb-reporting listening to this service, so the award writes an outbox row in the same transaction as the lot update. The plan's pattern set for the key is DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19, so DP-09 (outbox and inbox library, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON) is absent, and the H row carries no library story. The service schema holds outbox_event as a library object and the award is published once per lot and decision on rwb.debtsale.events.v1 with no personal data; the absent library row is recorded rather than added to the metadata.
evidence: TSD S6 T5.3 row LotAwarded Published; context pack S6 ownership rows Events (1) EV-23 and slide 13 row P8 Payment (E on S6) and row P9 Reporting (E on S6); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 row (H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); WP B2-S6-008 patterns [DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19] and H without the library row
proposed: Publish rwb.debtsale.LotAwarded.v1 from the outbox in the award transaction, keep the H row as the plan states it, and record RWB-PLT-TE006-CON as the wave 0 library the topic and the consumer contracts need

title: RWB-S6-E6005: the run's extract folder holds no FSD or TSD extract for module S6, so the module files stand in
source: Template and Rules v1 R7.3 and R9; WP B2-S6-008 read list (extract files of the FSD and TSD folders whose name contains S6); _work/msr/extract listing; FSD S6 Debt sale v3; TSD S6 Debt sale v2; legacy RWB-E6-005
description: The WP tells the worker to read the extract files of the FSD and TSD folders whose name contains S6, and the extract folder holds no S6 module file; it carries the Program, Epic 1, Epic 2, Epics 3 to 8, Business Rules and Routing Logic, Architecture v5, Temporal and Drools, Event and Messaging, Batch and Scheduling, LDM, NFS, ADR, Decision Log and API Specification extracts only. The module documents exist under the requirements folders and are the sources the extract would have carried, so they are read directly and the fill order of R7.3 is unchanged. The effect is documentation only: no value changes.
evidence: _work/msr/extract listing contains no file with S6 or Debt sale in its name; FSD S6 Debt sale v3 sits in the FSD by Module v6 folder and TSD S6 Debt sale v2 in the Technical Specifications by Module v5 folder; Template and Rules v1 R7.3 fill order
proposed: Read the FSD S6 v3 and TSD S6 v2 module files directly, cite them as the module source in section 18, and add the S6 extract pair at the next extract pass

title: RWB-S6-E6005: EP06 puts the story in wave 4 and release 30 April 2027 while rwb-debtsale is an Architecture v5 wave 3 service
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.6 (W-MAP), R5.7 and R9; WP B2-S6-008 story lines (wave, release); context pack S6 (service wave 3); FSD S6 Debt sale v3 A2.9 (first in E6); legacy RWB-E6-005 (Epic E6, release 30 April 2027)
section: Metadata (Wave, Release, Business epic); Sections 2, 3 and 19
description: RWB-E6-005 belongs to business epic EP06, whose W-MAP wave is 4, while rwb-debtsale is created in wave 3 in the context pack and the platform table. Rule R5.6 keeps the W-MAP wave only when it is earlier than the service wave, and here it is later, so the two sources point in different directions and the story is stated in wave 4 with release 30 April 2027 as the plan gives it. One service therefore delivers its EP05 keys in wave 3 and this key in wave 4. The date is copied unchanged and marked tentative by U7 and is not raised as a gap.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R4 service table S6 wave 3 and R5.6 W-MAP EP06 wave 4; context pack S6 wave 3; WP B2-S6-008 wave 4 release 30 April 2027; legacy RWB-E6-005 Epic row E6, release 30 April 2027
proposed: Keep wave 4 and the 30 April 2027 release as the plan and the legacy epic give them, and ask the wave planner to state in the wave map that rwb-debtsale delivers its EP05 keys in wave 3 and its EP06 keys in wave 4

title: RWB-S6-E6005: the four legacy criteria span three sibling stories, R-DS-23 confirms the award, and the requirement mapping differs between the FSD and the TSD
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 and R9; legacy RWB-E6-005 AC1 to AC4; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-04, R-DS-19, R-DS-20 and R-DS-23; TSD S6 Debt sale v2 T4, T-A.1 and T8; FSD S6 Debt sale v3 A2.9 and requirements served; WP B2-S6-008 slice RWB-S6-E6005-APP (acs AC1 to AC4)
description: (1) Legacy AC2 owns R-DS-19 (BIDS_RECEIVED to AWARD_PENDING) and legacy AC3 owns R-DS-04 (LOT_BUILT to LOT_WITH_COMMITTEE): the first is this story's price test, the second is the priced-lot step built by RWB-S6-E5024-APP and approved by RWB-S6-E6001-APP. (2) Legacy AC1's award with the approval the limit requires is the P4 DoA test and the P7 chain, while R-DS-23 confirms the award, generates the sale agreement and the notices, and moves the case to LOT_AWARDED under RWB-S6-E6006-APP. (3) The legacy endpoint row POST /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}/award is API-S6-003, while the lot read API-S6-002 is RWB-S6-E6001-APP's and the data-room operations are RWB-S6-E5026-APP's. (4) FSD S6 gives the award as FEAT-DBS-09 with REQ-S6-006 (Must, E6), while TSD S6 T8 maps REQ-S6-006 to FEAT-DBS-05.
evidence: legacy RWB-E6-005 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4 and Endpoints row; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DS-19, R-DS-20, R-DS-04 and R-DS-23; TSD S6 T4 rows R-DS-19 and R-DS-23; TSD S6 T-A.1 API-S6-003 first in E6; TSD S6 T8 row REQ-S6-006 to FEAT-DBS-05; FSD S6 A1.2 row FEAT-DBS-09 epic E6 and requirements served REQ-S6-006
area: Rule, criterion, endpoint and requirement ownership
proposed: Keep the four criteria word for word, build the price test, the award route and the buyer columns here, name R-DS-04's effect with RWB-S6-E5024-APP and RWB-S6-E6001-APP, name R-DS-23 and the agreement with RWB-S6-E6006-APP, and trace REQ-S6-006 with the TSD mapping difference recorded

title: RWB-S6-E6005: no column or field holds the bid or the award price, the buyer-class rule and the score field IDs are unstated, and the score is a view only rwb-source-data may read
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5, R7.3 and R9; TSD S6 Debt sale v2 T3.1, T3.2, T4 and T5.2; FSD S6 Debt sale v3 A2.9.3.1, A2.9.3.2 and requirements served; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DS-19; context pack S6 (slide 13, ownership rows); legacy RWB-E6-005 Data table; Architecture v5 slides 29, 37 and 45
description: (1) R-DS-19 tests the best bid against the reserve and the 54 percent cap, and API-S6-003 awards a lot to a buyer, but TSD S6 T3.1 defines no bid table and no bid or award-price column on debt_sale_lot or debt_sale_account; only selling_price (DF-SAL-036) exists, and no source states that the award writes it or how a bid is allocated across accounts. (2) No source states how buyer_class is derived from the buyer, and the 54 percent cap is a rule value with a version, not a constant. (3) The legacy Data table reads the model score from v_ace_score; the target gives the 30 v_ace_* views to rwb-source-data alone and rwb-debtsale holds no view grant, and no source gives the field IDs of the score data product. (4) The FSD field catalog of A2.9.3.2 lists eight lot fields and omits payment_terms and status, which the TSD carries.
evidence: FSD S6 A2.9.3.1 row R-DS-19 (54 percent cap) and A2.9.3.2 field catalog (eight fields, no bid amount); TSD S6 T3.1 debt_sale_lot DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-030 and debt_sale_account DF-SAL-031 to DF-SAL-037; TSD S6 T3.2 lists; legacy RWB-E6-005 Data table row v_ace_score DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279; Architecture v5 slide 29 and slide 37 (views read only by rwb-source-data); context pack slide 13 and ownership rows
area: Data model, reference values and ACE boundary
proposed: Carry the best bid, its time and the price achieved in the decision record and the operation contracts, write only buyer_partner_id and buyer_class on the lot, read the cap and the reserve rule with their package version, and confirm the score data product and its field IDs before the contract is tagged
